author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Gold moved modestly higher early Thursday as a weaker U.S. dollar supported demand and investors awaited inflation reports that could reshape expectations for Federal Reserve policy, Reuters reported.

At the time of the Reuters update, spot gold was up 0.3% at $4,414.28 an ounce. December U.S. gold futures were down 0.1% at $4,457.20. Those figures are a dated market snapshot, not live prices, and can change throughout the trading session.

The U.S. producer-price index is due Thursday, followed by consumer inflation data Friday. Both reports will be watched for evidence that higher energy and transportation costs are feeding into broader prices. Interest-rate expectations affect gold because bullion pays no yield, while moves in the dollar change its cost for holders of other currencies.

Reuters said most economists expect the Fed to hold rates at its September meeting and through year-end, while market pricing showed a different view, assigning a 60% chance of an increase this month. That gap makes the inflation releases particularly important for bonds, currencies, precious metals and rate-sensitive stocks.
dek: A softer dollar supported bullion early Thursday while investors watched producer- and consumer-price reports for clues on interest rates.
headline: Gold edges higher as markets await U.S. inflation data
